consumption.n: Atlas estimate: apparent consumption of refined copper in 2024, by country: production plus imports minus exports of the same product and year, in kt. Production: refined copper production, primary and secondary (USGS), USGS MCS 2026 2024 column. Imports and exports: CEPII BACI 2024, refined copper (HS 7403), gross weight, with the atlas's cleaning rules, summed before any rounding. Trade is refined copper only (HS 7403, cathodes and refined forms); HS 7402, unrefined copper and anodes that refineries import, is left out. Refinery output counts primary and secondary refined copper, trade in scrap is not known. Stock changes are not known, so this is apparent consumption, not measured use. Only the countries for which USGS gives production are listed (17); this is not a ranking of the world's consumers. 4 of them are left out for want of a customs row (no import row: Australia, Chile, DR Congo, Zambia): the extract omits flows below 1,000 t and 1 million USD, so this is a small flow or none, not a gap in USGS production, and it is not counted as zero; 0 are left out because the result is negative. Not listed because USGS names no production for them: the largest of them by customs net imports (imports minus exports) are Italy 525 kt, Taiwan 508 kt, Turkey 380 kt, Thailand 317 kt, Brazil 281 kt, Malaysia 256 kt. Their apparent consumption is that plus their own production, which USGS does not name (it may sit in its 'Other countries' line): they are absent because the table needs a production figure, not because they consume less than the countries listed. World: the world production of the same product in 2024 as USGS gives it (27,600 kt, the sum of its countries and its 'Other countries' line): trade nets out in the world, so apparent consumption of the world is its production apart from changes in stocks, which are not known. The shares are computed on it, and 'Countries not listed' is the world total minus the countries listed.

notes: Refined copper (HS 7403, 7402), 2024 (CEPII BACI): world 12.08 Mt gross weight; top exporters DR Congo 2.21 Mt, Chile 2.16 Mt, Zambia 1.08 Mt.

Chile's copper concentrate: customs data declare some of it at 3,988 to 10,220 USD per tonne in 2024, against about 2,195 for Peru's concentrate to the same destinations; a tonnage declared in contained copper rather than gross weight is a plausible cause, not established here. Where Chile's unit value is more than 1.8 times Peru's (to the same destination when Peru ships 50 kt or more there, otherwise Peru's average of the year), the tonnage is an Atlas estimate: the declared value divided by Peru's unit value times 1.125, the median ratio of Chile's unit value to Peru's in the 10 years in which Chile's declarations are in line (2002, 2009, 2014 to 2020 and 2023). Chile then exports 12.44 Mt instead of the 4.95 Mt declared, and Chile to China 8.24 Mt instead of 2.79 Mt. Importers' own declarations (UN Comtrade) would measure it; the atlas has no access key for them.

Trade tables are copper ores and concentrates in gross weight (Mt), not contained copper; USGS production is contained copper (kt Cu). The refinery table is USGS refined copper production (primary and secondary).

Customs data record 0.492 Mt of refined copper from Zambia to Switzerland in 2024 (45.6% of Zambia's recorded exports and 99.2% of Switzerland's recorded imports, CEPII BACI). Switzerland has no coast and is a trading centre for commodities, so the cargo probably ends elsewhere and the customs record only the declared country: a possible reading, not established here. The tonnes stay in the tables and are counted at the passages of the route to its declared destination; no generated route is built from this pair.

The 'refined and blister copper' tables add HS 7403 (refined copper, 10.0 Mt in 2024) and HS 7402 (unrefined copper and anodes, 2.0 Mt, the feed of refineries). The apparent consumption table uses HS 7403 only.
